cyclosporin is an extremely powerful, non-toxic immunosuppressing agent in dogs and pigs.
cyclosporin is an extremely potent and non-toxic immunosuppressive drug in experimental animals and is currently being tested in man.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of agents which are immunosuppressive in man, but which do not produce serious side-effects.
the development of new agents and the evaluation of new models for the investigation of immunosuppressive agents.
the development of a model for testing immunosuppressants relevant to man.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immunosuppressive properties of these four agents in the laboratory are not predictive of clinical efficacy.
no agent is yet available which is sufficiently powerful, non-toxic and reliable in man for routine use.
none of the agents investigated is suitable as an immunosuppessant in man.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the search for a potent, specific, non-toxic immunosuppressing agent continues.
cyclosporin appears to be the most potent immunosuppressive drug yet described, but the search for a suitable model to evaluate the activity of new agents in man must continue.
the search for the ideal immunosuppressive drug continues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immunosuppressive effects of drugs can only be evaluated by testing them in the most relevant model possible.
the immunosuppressive effects of these agents are only partially predictable from the effects of the same agents on immunological parameters measured in the laboratory.
it is difficult to extrapolate from animal experiments to man and that clinical trials must be undertaken in patients.
